title: The Boxes Stay, the Labels Change

scenes.tts: Mate two yellow mice as often as you like, and you will never get a yellow mouse that breeds true. That looked like a failure of Mendel's rules. It was not. For unlinked genes, segregation and independent assortment keep working in every case here. What changes is the map from genotype to phenotype.
scenes.visual: Two yellow mice are crossed and their young include non-yellow ones, so a true-breeding yellow line is crossed out. Mendel's rules flash red, then turn green, and a map arrow joins genotype to phenotype.
scenes.narration: Mate two yellow mice as often as you like, and you will never get a yellow mouse that breeds true. That looked like a failure of Mendel's rules. It was not. scenes.tts: Cross red snapdragons with white ones, and every F one flower is pink. This is incomplete dominance. Self the pink plants, and red and white come back, at one red, two pink, one white. Nothing blended, because a pink plant is a heterozygote. In Mendel's peas the one to two to one was hidden, but here the colours show it plainly.
scenes.visual: Red and white flowers give a pink F1. A two by two square of allele dots fills with red, pink, pink and white flowers, tallied 1 : 2 : 1. The pink flowers briefly turn red as if one allele hid the other, then back.
scenes.caption: Cross red snapdragons with white ones, and every F1 flower is pink. This is incomplete dominance. Self the pink plants, and red and white come back, at 1 red, 2 pink, 1 white. scenes.tts: Now back to the yellow mouse, whose yellow allele is dominant for coat colour but recessive for survival. A mouse with two copies dies before implantation, so one quarter of the conceptions die. The survivors are two yellow to one black, so twelve live pups should be eight yellow and four black. Every live yellow mouse is therefore a heterozygote. That is why none breeds true.
scenes.visual: The same square with yellow and black alleles. Three boxes become mice, the double-yellow box dies and is crossed out, the survivors are tallied 2 : 1, twelve pups appear as eight yellow and four black, and the yellow mice show one yellow and one black allele.
scenes.caption: Now back to the yellow mouse, whose yellow allele is dominant for coat colour but recessive for survival. Every live yellow mouse is therefore a heterozygote. That is why none breeds true.

scenes.tts: When two genes act on one trait, a genotype at one can hide the other, which is called epistasis. In Labrador retrievers, a dominant B makes black pigment, and its recessive form makes brown, called chocolate. Cross two black dogs heterozygous at both genes, and the sixteen boxes sort into the usual four classes. But a dog with two copies of the recessive form of E has a yellow coat, whatever its B genotype. So the last two classes merge, and the ratio is nine black, three chocolate, four yellow.
scenes.visual: A four by four square of BbEe gametes. The sixteen boxes colour into nine, three, three and one. The ee block lights up, the last two classes turn yellow together, and the tally reads 9 black, 3 chocolate, 4 yellow.

scenes.tts: Other interactions regroup the same sixteen boxes. If both genes need a dominant allele to make colour, the ratio is nine to seven. If a dominant allele at one gene hides the other, the ratio is twelve to three to one. If a dominant allele at either gene is enough, the ratio is fifteen to one. In every case, only the labels on the boxes change.
scenes.visual: The same sixteen genotypes are recoloured in turn into 9 : 7, 12 : 3 : 1 and 15 : 1, with the genotype letters unchanged.

scenes.tts: The boxes never changed, only their labels. One allele hides the other, and you see three to one. Neither hides, you see one to two to one, and if one class dies, you see two to one. Keep this rule. Segregation keeps working in every case here, and only the map from genotype to phenotype changes.
scenes.visual: One fixed two by two square is relabelled in turn as 3 : 1, 1 : 2 : 1 and 2 : 1, then a genotype to phenotype arrow with the map highlighted.
scenes.caption: The boxes never changed, only their labels. One allele hides the other, and you see 3:1. Neither hides, you see 1:2:1, and if one class dies, you see 2:1. Keep this rule. Segregation keeps working in every case here, and only the map from genotype to phenotype changes.
